The '''Alomara''' is a desert spanning across [[Quia]]. With an area of 7,491,042 square  kilometres (4,654,717 sq mi), it is the largest hot desert in the world and the largest desert overall. The name "Alomara" is derived from [[Verstian Language|Verstian]]: Alomra, a broken plural form of aloma', meaning "desert".

The desert covers much of [[Quia]], excluding the fertile region on the [[Fedaea|Fedaean]] Sea coast, the [[# Kertesen Mountain range|Kertesen]] and[[Inas|Inas Mountain]] ranges, and the [[Ghotchwe]] Valley in [[United Mihili]] and the [[Zhanshe]]. It stretches from [[Fedaea]] in the east and the [[Kertesen Mountain range]] in the north to the [[Haanian Ocean]] in the west, where the landscape gradually changes from desert to coastal hills. To the south, it is bounded by the [[Quian steppe]], a belt of semi-dry tropical grasslands around the[[Ukliqui River|Ukliqui River valley]] and the Volvern region of sub-Alomaran Qiua.

For several hundred thousand years, the Alomara has alternated between desert and savanna grassland in a 20,000-year cycle caused by the precession of Earth's axis (about 26,000 years) as it rotates around the Sun.
==Geography==
The Alomara spans much of the [[Far lands]], [[United Mihili]], and [[Zhanshe]]. and reaches into southern [[Anymna]] and western [[Finae]], [[Myla]] and [[Volver]]. Covering about 7,491,042 million square kilometres (4,654,717 sq mi), it comprises roughly 25% of Quia; by including all regions receiving under 250 mm (9.8 in) of annual precipitation, its extent would approach  8,021,000 million square kilometres (4,984,018 sq mi). It is one of the principal physiographic provinces of the Quian massive, and its size and reflectivity make it theoretically detectable from distant star systems with near-current observational technology.

Contrary to popular belief, most of the Alomara consists of [[wikipedia:Hamada|rocky hamada]], with large [[wikipedia:wiki/Dune|sand-dune]] fields representing only a limited portion of its area, though individual dunes can exceed 175 metres. Wind and rare rainfall generate features such as dunes, gravel plains, [[wikipedia:Wadi|dry valleys (wadi)]], ephemeral lake beds, and [[wikipedia:Salt_flat|salt flats]]. Notable landforms include the [[Cokaowa Structure]] in [[United Mihili]]. Several isolated mountain ranges, many volcanic.

The central Alomara is hyperarid and largely barren, while its northern and southern margins and highlands support sparse grasslands and shrubs, with trees concentrated in wadis. Extreme subregions such as the  [[Zoekal Desert]] may experience years without rainfall. To the east, the Alomara borders [[Ankran|Ankran ecoregion]], with its limit corresponding to the northern boundary of [[kak]] cultivation, the southern limit of grass, and the 100 mm annual rainfall. To the south, it transitions into the [[Quian steppe]], marked by the ranges of drought-tolerant species.

Major cities within the desert include [[Arindor]], [[Kilduva]], [[Hralen]], and [[Tamnar]]; [[Shetava]]; [[Varkunadishal]]; [[Mavoni]]; and [[Zundekhei]].
==Climate==
The Alomara is the world’s largest [[wikipedia:Desert|hot desert]], situated beneath the subtropical ridge in the horse latitudes, where descending warm, dry air suppresses cloud formation. This persistent subsidence creates a highly stable atmosphere with virtually no rainfall, producing the region's characteristic [[wikipedia:Desert_climate|hot desert climate]] (Köppen BWh). The eastern Alomara, especially the [[Zoekal Desert]], experiences the strongest subsidence and is among the driest and sunniest places on [[Andah]].

Rainfall in the southern Alomara and stepp originates primarily from the seasonal migration of the [[wikipedia:Intertropical_Convergence_Zone|Intertropical Convergence Zone]], but precipitation remains brief, irregular, and limited. The desert’s climate is marked by extremely low and erratic rainfall, high temperatures and sunshine levels, minimal humidity, strong diurnal temperature ranges, and some of the highest potential evaporation rates recorded globally.
===Temperature===
The Alomara Desert experiences exceptionally high [[wikipedia:Solar_irradiance|solar exposure]] due to typically clear skies, resulting in extremely long sunshine duration. Most of the desert receives over 3,600 hours of bright sunshine annually, which is more than 82% of daylight hours, with large areas in the east exceeding 4,000 hours (over 91% of daylight hours). This significant solar incidence translates to an annual average direct [[wikipedia:Solar_irradiance|solar irradiation]] of approximately 2,800 kWh/(m2⋅year), indicating immense potential for [[wikipedia:Solar_power|solar energy production]]. The combination of the sun's high position, extremely [[wikipedia:Humidity|low relative humidity]], and the absence of vegetation and rainfall establishes the Great Desert as the hottest large region globally, and in some areas, the hottest place on Andah during summer.

Average high temperatures generally surpass 38 to 40 °C (100.4 to 105.0 °F) during the hottest month, except at the highest altitudes. [[wikipedia:Heat_wave|Extreme heat]] is exemplified by the world's highest mean monthly maximum temperature of 47 °C (116.6 °F) recorded in [[Zhanshe]]. Sand and ground temperatures can be even more intense, easily reaching 80 °C (176 °F) or more. Due to the lack of cloud cover and very low humidity, the desert exhibits high diurnal temperature variations, with nighttime temperatures typically 13 °C  to 20 °C (23 °F  to 36 °F) cooler than daytime highs. While the myth of "especially cold" nights after "extremely hot" days is inaccurate, winter nights can drop to or below the freezing point, particularly in high-elevation areas.
